# `sensor_surface`

the channels as a surface, a triangulated helmet whose vertices are the picked channels, a manifold derived from the channels with its vertex-to-channel map.

Version 1, scope `subject`. Run it with `nxr-neuro run sensor_surface --dataset <folder> --subject <id> ...`; `nxr-neuro run sensor_surface --help` prints the same options.

Examples:

```
nxr-neuro run sensor_surface --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --channels <channels manifold> --pick <indices selection of it> [--name NAME] [--position-rule stored] [--cut 2]
```

## Inputs

| input | what it is | required |
|---|---|---|
| `channels` | manifold points, where {"name": "$channels"} (name the channels manifold (--channels)) | yes |
| `pick` | selection indices, manifold channels.manifold.0, where {"name": "$pick"} (name an indices selection of the channels: the surface's vertices and their order (--pick)) | yes |

## Parameters

Each is an option `--<name> VALUE` (dashes for underscores; the value is read as YAML) or `--set NAME=VALUE`.

| parameter | option | default | unit | choices | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `channels` | `--channels` | `required` | - |  | the channels manifold (a points manifold) by name |
| `pick` | `--pick` | `required` | - |  | an indices selection of the channels by name: which channels are the vertices, in which order |
| `name` | `--name` | `{channels}_surface` | - |  | the surface's name; its map is <name>_map |
| `position_rule` | `--position-rule` | `brainstorm` | - | brainstorm, stored | a channel's position: brainstorm (the mean of its first coil_points coil points; its stored point without coils) or stored (its stored point) |
| `coil_points` | `--coil-points` | `4` | points |  | how many of a channel's first coil points are averaged (Brainstorm: 4) |
| `cut` | `--cut` | `2.0` | - |  | a triangle is removed when one of its edges is cut x the median edge or longer (nxr: 2) |
| `pole` | `--pole` | `[0, 0, 1]` | - |  | the projection's pole, a direction in the channels' coordinate system (nxr: +z) |
| `orientation` | `--orientation` | `outward` | - | outward, as_triangulated | each triangle turned so that its normal points away from the sensors' centroid (outward), or as_triangulated |
| `repair_passes` | `--repair-passes` | `20` | passes |  | the most passes of the pinch repair before refusing (nxr: 20) |

## The chain of nodes

| phase | node | in | with | out |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | [`meeg.channel_positions`](../nodes.md) | channels=channels, pick=pick | position_rule=$position_rule, coil_points=$coil_points | positions, channel_index |
| before | [`geometry.point_set_mesh`](../nodes.md) | points=positions | cut=$cut, pole=$pole, orientation=$orientation, repair_passes=$repair_passes | faces |
| before | [`geometry.surface_from_parts`](../nodes.md) | vertices=positions, faces=faces |  | surface |

`before` steps run once, `chunks` steps run on every chunk of the recording, `after` steps run once on what the chunks accumulated.

## Outputs

| output | stored as |
|---|---|
| `surface` | kind manifold, type surface, name $name, derived_from channels.manifold.0 |
| `channel_index` | kind field, kind_name channel map, name {name}_map, on surface |

## Notes from the definition

```text
THE SENSOR SURFACE: the channels given a geometry, a triangulated helmet whose vertices ARE the channels. A manifold DERIVED from the channels by its own definition (as `glue`
makes the glued cortex): vertex i is the channel `<name>_map`[i] of the channels manifold, so a field on those channels is a field on the surface's vertices with no mapping, and the
channels get what any surface has: the intrinsic complex and its operators, the Hodge-Dirac modes (`run eigenmodes --surface <name>`; the helmet is an open disc), the heat distance,
and neighbourhood selections, before any inverse model.

THE GRAPH:  channels (a points manifold, coils when stored), pick (an indices selection of it) --[meeg.channel_positions]--> positions [n x 3], channel_index [n];
            positions --[geometry.point_set_mesh]--> faces [F x 3];  positions, faces --[geometry.surface_from_parts]--> surface.
Stored: the surface `<name>` (type surface, derived from the channels manifold; its producer records the pick, the position rule and the mesher's options and report) and the
map `<name>_map` (an integer field on the surface: each vertex's channel).
WHICH CHANNELS is the caller's: the pick names them and their order (e.g. the channels a cross-spectrum or a kernel was made on, `<name>_channels`); --channels and --pick are REQUIRED
(their default is `required`, which the reader refuses to run with).
Positions: Brainstorm's rule by default (the mean of a channel's first four coil points: a CTF axial gradiometer's pickup coil), or the stored point (named: position_rule stored).
The mesh: nxr's sensor mesh (the projection about the pole, the planar Delaunay, long chords cut, pinches and holes repaired, every triangle turned outward); a point in no triangle
is refused.

What it cannot resolve: the surface is a triangulation of the sensors, not a physical surface: its geometry is the helmet's layout (the sensors' spacing is its resolution: no
pattern shorter than about two sensor spacings is resolved on it), and a field on it is the sensors' measurement (lead fields, not cortical currents).

  nxr-neuro run sensor_surface --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --channels <channels manifold> --pick <indices selection of it> [--name NAME] [--position-rule stored] [--cut 2]
```
